blocks.h2: How to Test Your Sump Pump Before Spring
blocks.body: Lift the lid and pour a bucket of water into the pit. The float should rise, the pump should start, empty the pit and shut off on its own. Then go outside and make sure water comes out of the discharge pipe and drains away from the house. If the pump hums but doesn't move water, runs and won't stop or doesn't start at all, call us. Spring rain is a bad time to find out.

blocks.h2: Where Your Sump Pump Water Goes
blocks.body: A sump pump is only as good as its discharge line. If the line dumps water right next to the foundation, it can cycle back into the pit. If it freezes in winter, the pump can't empty the pit. We check that the line carries water well away from the house and slopes properly, and add a freeze guard fitting where it helps.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Can you install a sump pump in an older basement?
items.answer: Often. We cut a pit where water collects and route the discharge outside.

items.q: Do I need a battery backup?
items.preview: If the basement is finished, yes.
items.answer: If the basement is finished or stores anything valuable, yes.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
Will a sump pump stop sewer backups?
items.answer: No. It moves groundwater. For sewer backups, see overhead sewers or backflow valves.

items.q: Why does my sump pump run when it hasn't rained?
items.answer: High groundwater can keep it running. So can a failed check valve that lets water flow back into the pit.

items.q: Can you install a sump pump with an alarm?
items.answer: Yes. A high-water alarm warns you if the pump falls behind.

items.q: How much does sump pump installation cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and pit. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, whether you need a new pit and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
